subject: Conditional rebate request + SLA addendum — Orbis Health pilot
messages:
From: Alison Reyes <alison.reyes@orbishealth.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: conditional rebate + SLA addendum for enterprise pilot

Hi Lukas / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Orbis is very interested in moving the 3-month pilot forward, but procurement has one item they want to surface before we finalize commercials. The pilot will be used across three inpatient products and we need a slightly more aggressive pricing profile for the ramp months in exchange for a commitment to convert to a yearly commitment if we hit the usage thresholds.

High level ask: a layered rebate structure that starts at 25% off list for months 1–3, stepping to 10% off for months 4–12, plus an SLA addendum with a 99.5% availability commitment and incident response TTR definitions. Procurement wants the rebate built into the MSA (not a separate credit memo) and a clause that allows a revenue clawback if conversion to annual commitment does not occur.

I attached the RFP and a procurement checklist for reference (orbis_procurement_RFP.xlsx). Can you confirm whether this is something Redwood can approve at the VP/CFO level and what the internal path would look like? We need a signed term sheet by the end of March to make the quarter plan.

Best,
Alison Reyes
Director, Strategic Procurement
Orbis Health

Marissa / Aditya / Kim — looping you on an incoming procurement ask from Orbis. Summary: they want a steeper up-front rebate (25% first 3 months) in exchange for a commit-to-convert clause and an SLA addendum. Procurement insists rebate be in the MSA and wants clawback language.

Quick thoughts:
- We can consider a time-bound promotional rebate but should avoid open-ended list reductions.
- Prefer structured tiers tied to usage (e.g., 0–200M tokens: 25% pilot rebate; 200M–1B: 10% for remainder of year) with explicit conversion criteria.
- Require finance signoff for material margin impact and legal to draft clawback language.
- VP Sales or CRO signoff + CFO countersignature for any rebate >15% over the first 6 months.

I drafted a starting term sheet and attached (orb_draft_term_sheet_v1.pdf). Please review margin impact and legal risk examples. We should aim to get an internal memo (one page) that I can route to VP Sales and CFO for approval.

Lukas
Head of Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 08:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: conditional rebate + SLA addendum for enterprise pilot

Lukas — thanks for the quick draft. I think this is one we can win but we should tighten a few things before taking it up to VP/CFO: 

1) Structure recommendation (commercial):
   - Pilot rebate: 20% for months 1–3 (on committed monthly floor), stepping to 10% months 4–12. 
   - Conversion trigger: convert to 12-month annual contract if average monthly committed usage >= 80% of projected ramp for two consecutive months.
   - Clawback: 100% revenue clawback pro-rated over months still remaining in the first-year term if conversion does not happen within 45 days of pilot end.

2) Operational asks (SLA/ops):
   - Add a narrow SLA addendum for pilot customers: target 99.5% uptime for inference endpoints and defined response windows for Sev1/Sev2.

3) Approval path & risk:
   - Recommend VP Sales approval + CFO countersign for any effective rebate >18% in month 1–3.
   - Legal (Kim) to confirm that we can model the clawback as a recoverable credit vs. an amendment that permanently reduces list.

I can draft the one-page memo for VP/CFO if you give the green light on the 20%/10% ladder and the 45-day conversion window. Also suggest we attach a brief financial model (Aditya) and an ops impact note (Kim).

- Marissa
VP, Commercial Strategy
Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 16:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: conditional rebate + SLA addendum for enterprise pilot

Team — ran the numbers on the proposed 20%/10% ladder. High-level financials attached (financial_model_ORB-2027-02.xlsx). Key points: 

- NPV over 24 months with a conservative 50% conversion probability: +$160k net (post-rebate) given Orbis' projected usage profile — deal is accretive if conversion occurs.
- If conversion fails and clawback is triggered, median worst-case revenue recovery is ~70% after collection costs; still better than walking away but more manual collection work.
- Recommend approving a limited promotional rebate: 20% for months 1–3 capped at $150k absolute rebate exposure, then 10% for months 4–12. Include clawback with 90-day recovery window and a set-off right in the MSA.

If you want, I can produce a one-page finance memo for the VP/CFO that shows scenario analysis (best/likely/worst).

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Director, Revenue Finance
Redwood Inference

Approvals requested: VP Sales signoff + CFO countersignature (for rebate >18% during launch). Legal: confirm clawback wording and set-off mechanics. Ops: confirm SLA feasibility for pilot scope.

Attachments: draft term sheet; finance scenario analysis; procurement RFP.
